It is easy to divine with what sense of grief the faction saw its nest disturbed so suddenly. First there was huge trepidation, then cries: on one side torments and mournful laments of those who deplored the persecution of truth and innocence; on the other side, curses of those who denounced all that was of sacred and profane dignity; finally, there was tumult among the very parts of the faction, and it was contested for many years of the present century. For since they were everywhere urged to subscription by the vigilance of the Bishops

Those who were of a more tender conscience, or wished to appear so, looked around for subterfuges and means by which they might mitigate the horror of perjury, and they took refuge in equivocations and mental restrictions, which even the most lax Morality would abhor.
